title: Pollution Prevention
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: When it rains, stormwater picks up sediment, chemicals and debris from a construction site and carries them to storm sewers and waterways. This talk covers what crews must do to keep pollutants on site.
talking_points: Rain washes over loose soil and materials stored outside. It can carry sediment, debris and chemicals into storm sewers, rivers, lakes or coastal waters.
Common site pollutants include sediment, solid and sanitary wastes, oil and grease, concrete truck washout, construction chemicals, construction debris, phosphorus, nitrogen and pesticides.
A Clean Water Act permit is required when construction disturbs 1 acre or more, or less than 1 acre if it is part of a common plan that will disturb 1 or more acres.
Design, install and maintain effective erosion and sediment controls and pollution prevention measures.
Stabilize disturbed areas immediately when work has stopped and will not resume for more than 14 days.
Do not discharge concrete washout wastewater unless it is managed by an appropriate control. The same goes for washout or cleanout of stucco, paint and form release oils.
Do not discharge fuels, oils or other vehicle pollutants. Do not use soaps or solvents to wash vehicles and equipment.
Do not discharge dewatering water unless it is managed by appropriate controls.
site_hazards_to_check: Loose soil or stockpiles with no erosion or sediment controls
Materials, chemicals or fuel stored outside where rain can reach them
Concrete, stucco or paint washout done without an approved control
Vehicle or equipment washing with soap or solvents
Disturbed areas left open for more than 14 days
discussion_questions: Where does the water go when it rains on our site, and what would it pick up on the way?
Where is our concrete washout area, and does everyone know to use it?
Which disturbed areas on this job have been idle and need to be stabilized?

attribution.notice: Adapted from EPA's Stormwater Discharges from Construction Activities page. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by EPA.

flags: Content is quote-accurate to EPA Stormwater Discharges from Construction Activities (1 acre / common plan, 14-day stabilization, washout, fuels, soaps/solvents, dewatering, pollutant list). Public domain, epa.gov, notice preserved.

OSHA mapping: no OSHA 1926 standard governs stormwater. The General Duty Clause entry is nominal and should not be read as an OSHA requirement; the real basis is the Clean Water Act / 40 CFR 450.21 (C&D rule). Non-blocking: structurer may note this in osha_standards or a note field. Judgment: an environmental site-controls talk is acceptable in a construction toolbox library because crews perform these tasks (washout, dewatering, stockpiles).

Legal caution (non-blocking): point 3 states the permit requirement flatly. Permit authority varies (EPA CGP vs state programs); crews should defer to the project's SWPPP/permit. Not an OSHA-accuracy defect. No UK wording.
